flashcards.q: Name SageMaker's four inference modes and their key limits.
flashcards.a: Real-time endpoint (25MB payload, 60s/8min streaming, no scale-to-zero), Serverless Inference (4MB, 60s, scales to zero, cold start), Async Inference (1GB, up to 1hr, scales to zero, queued), Batch Transform (no endpoint, offline dataset scoring).

flashcards.q: Bedrock on-demand vs Provisioned Throughput -- decision rule?
flashcards.a: On-demand: pay per token, no commitment, wins at low/spiky volume. Provisioned Throughput: flat $/hour per model unit, wins ONLY when sustained on-demand cost at your actual throughput exceeds the flat rate -- idle provisioned hours still bill in full.

flashcards.q: What's required to invoke a fine-tuned model on Bedrock?
flashcards.a: Provisioned Throughput -- you cannot serve a fine-tuned model on Bedrock via on-demand pricing.

flashcards.q: What hidden cost do naive self-hosted-LLM-vs-API comparisons routinely omit?
flashcards.a: Ops labor: a production self-hosted fleet needs a commonly-cited minimum of 10-20 engineer-hours/month for maintenance, monitoring, and incident response, at $75-150/hr -- an extra $750-3,000/month before counting any incident.

flashcards.q: What is AgentCore and what does it add over the earlier Bedrock Agents builder?
flashcards.a: AWS's production agent runtime (GA mid-2026): session-isolated microVMs, filesystem persistence for suspend/resume, identity/auth wiring for tools, memory, and observability -- framework-agnostic infrastructure, versus Bedrock Agents' lower-code model+KB+action-group assembly.

flashcards.q: Kendra vs OpenSearch vs Bedrock Knowledge Bases -- one-line pick for each?
flashcards.a: Kendra: turnkey enterprise search UX with connectors and access control. OpenSearch: full retrieval-quality control (custom chunking, hybrid BM25+vector, reranking) at scale. Bedrock Knowledge Bases: zero-ops managed RAG pipeline (chunk/embed/retrieve/cite).

flashcards.q: Textract pricing spread across APIs on the same page?
flashcards.a: Roughly 47x: raw text detection ~$1.50/1,000 pages vs full forms+tables+queries analysis ~$70/1,000 pages on the identical document -- calling the wrong API is a common accidental bill inflator.

flashcards.q: When does a managed API (Comprehend/Textract/Transcribe/Rekognition) lose to a fine-tuned/self-hosted model?
flashcards.a: When the task needs domain-specific accuracy the generic model can't hit (specialized document layouts, niche entity taxonomies) AND volume is high enough to justify the fine-tuning/hosting investment -- try Custom Queries/Custom Classification first, since they close part of the gap without leaving the managed service.

flashcards.q: What does SageMaker Feature Store solve?
flashcards.a: Training/serving skew -- it gives an online (low-latency lookup) and offline (bulk training-time) store for the same feature definitions, so features computed for training match what's served at inference.

flashcards.q: Why is a SageMaker Serverless Inference endpoint's latency unpredictable?
flashcards.a: Cold starts -- it scales to zero when idle, and the first invocation after an idle gap pays a cold-start penalty to provision capacity, showing up as latency spikes correlated with traffic gaps rather than request complexity.

flashcards.q: Name the four core Bedrock Guardrails capabilities.
flashcards.a: Content filters (hate/insults/sexual/violence/misconduct/prompt attack, text and image), denied topics (natural-language definitions), sensitive information filters (PII types + custom regex, block or mask), and contextual grounding checks (scores output relevance/faithfulness to a source document).

flashcards.q: Why is this module explicitly flagged as the most volatile in the AWS Atlas?
flashcards.a: Foundation model pricing, provisioned-throughput rates, and agent-platform feature sets change on a timescale of months. The mental models (build-vs-buy arithmetic, inference-mode tradeoffs, retrieval decision tree) are durable; specific dollar figures and quotas must be re-verified before quoting in an interview.
